chunks: The making of anything of it did not cause Him any difficulty when He made it,
and the creation of anything which He created and formed did not fatigue Him.
He did not create it to heighten His authority
nor for fear of loss or harm,
nor to seek its help against an overwhelming foe,
nor to guard against any avenging opponent with its help,
nor for the extension of His domain by its help,
nor for boasting (over largeness of His possession) against a partner,
nor because He felt lonely and desired to seek its company.

key_terms.يَتَكَاءَدْهُ: to cause difficulty or fatigue to Him

ai.seo_question: Why did God create the world if He is self-sufficient?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha elaborates on the divine attribute of self-sufficiency (Al-Ghani) and the nature of creation. It asserts that God's act of creating the world was not driven by any need, such as alleviating loneliness, gaining strength, or increasing His dominion, but was a free act of will from one who lacks nothing. In Shia tafsir, this negation of 'need' (i'tiaz) is often contrasted with the concept of 'love' (mahabbah) as the true motive for creation, emphasizing that the Creator's actions are purely for the benefit of the created, not for His own enhancement.
